_readme: Every code path that moves a card into Triage, and the reason it writes on the card (DRE-7525). Read through scripts/triage_reasons.py; `python3 scripts/triage_reasons.py check` holds this file to the tree, and docs/triage-reasons.md is the page a person reads. The writes are discovered (ready_lane_writers.writes, located by green_light_rows.unit_of), never listed here: a `reasons` row names a discovered unit, the unit whose text carries its reason (`reason_at` — the unit itself or a discovered caller of it), an `anchor` that is a literal phrase of that reason or a constant the reasoning unit names and never the lane-write line, and a `note` saying what the reason tells a reader. A reason is a card comment, a `🔒 hold:` stamp, or the description of a card created directly in Triage. An `unreasoned` row names a unit that posts no reason today and says `why`; it is the gap list a follow-up card converts.

reasons.note: The card is created in Triage carrying the notice's own text, plus a line saying the console door was not reached and why.
A park note says nothing has read the card, why its classification could not be read, and that the way back is a move to Planning.
A park note says why Planning produced nothing — a stall, the planner line's bound or a hold nobody was asked about — and the way back.
The refusal names the description line that claims a dependency the board does not hold, and both fixes: set the relation or reword the line.
The watchdog's receipt says the card's repo is not on the dispatch rail and how to fix it, beside a no-route hold stamp naming the slug.
A hold stamp says the epic was sent back for a second re-review, and the hold's reason names the way back.

reasons.unit: agent-fix.yml#Escalate checks the loop structurally cannot fix
reasons.reason_at: agent-fix.yml#Escalate checks the loop structurally cannot fix
reasons.note: A card note names the red checks the fix loop cannot clear, beside an unfixable-check hold stamp at the head it read.
A fix-dispute hold stamp at the head says the fix loop's budget was spent on it and a pushed fix is the way back.
A plan-critic-bound hold stamp says the one-off critic's bound was reached, beside the critic's park note when it wrote one.

reasons.unit: plan.yml#First critic — the bound parks in Triage
reasons.reason_at: plan.yml#First critic — the bound parks in Triage
reasons.anchor: the plan goes on to neither the second critic nor Green Light
reasons.note: A park comment gives the first critic's finding this round and how to re-approve the plan once a person settles it.
The death note and record say the second critic's run died and how, and the park note after the move says what is owed.

reasons.unit: plan.yml#Review — the second critic passed a plan the first critic held
reasons.reason_at: plan.yml#Review — the second critic passed a plan the first critic held
reasons.note: A note read off the thread says the second critic passed a plan the first critic still held, so the two disagree.

reasons.unit: plan.yml#Review — the second critic produced no result
reasons.reason_at: plan.yml#Review — the second critic produced no result
reasons.anchor: The second critic could not decide on this plan
reasons.note: A park comment says the second critic could not decide on the plan as many times as the bound allows, so nobody has finished reading it.

reasons.unit: plan.yml#Re-check the revised plan — review mode
reasons.reason_at: plan.yml#Re-check the revised plan — review mode
reasons.anchor: but the revision did not pass the plan's own gates
reasons.note: A park comment says the planner's revision failed the plan's own gates, and which gate refused it.

reasons.unit: plan.yml#Review — the bound parks the plan in Triage
reasons.reason_at: plan.yml#Review — the bound parks the plan in Triage
reasons.anchor: nothing reaches Green Light until a person settles it
reasons.note: A park comment gives the second critic's finding, what the re-plan changed, and how to re-approve the plan once settled.
